newFindings.title: Race condition between parallel fix agents on shared branch
newFindings.description: When 4 parallel agents (I/J/K/L) all work on the same `fix/m18-doc-cleanup` branch in the same repo, git's stage-area is shared. Agent J's first commit accidentally swept in Agent L's pre-staged 03-* files; recovered via soft-reset + re-stage. Agent K reported an analogous race (02-* files absorbed into 03-* commit) but verified false on re-check.
newFindings.evidence: R3-A Agent J's recovery report; Agent K's report refuted by direct `git log --oneline` + `git show --stat` inspection of `ec31fe0c` (only 03-* files present, 02-* files in their own commit by Agent K). Pattern: when N agents share a working tree, the NEXT agent's safe default is to `git diff --cached --stat` before commit.
newFindings.scope: R3-A agents + future multi-agent same-branch dispatches

newFindings.title: Workspace root non-git + tool re-emission = silent corruption window
newFindings.description: `/Volumes/code/workspace/workspace.graph.json` was rewritten from id-keyed object to array on 2026-10-11 20:05 by an unidentified tool. The file lives in a non-git location, so no commit recorded the corruption. Consumers (audit / validate / MCP / registry-sync) silently parsed the malformed shape, producing 38 of 57 audit errors that only manifested when R2-A captured the error count.
newFindings.evidence: R2-A root-cause analysis + M19 defensive guard at `f0c17cf`. Pattern: critical non-git root files should have a daily shape-integrity check (or be moved to git for accountability).

newFindings.title: Bypass register is the durable record, not bypass-free
newFindings.description: 20 trailer-deficient M18 commits + 17 undocumented `--no-verify` commits landed on origin.
